title: Hospitality & Tourism Management
tagline: Run hotels, restaurants and attractions in the world's hospitality capital: guest experience, revenue, operations and Dubai's tourism rules.

superpower.name: Host Supreme
superpower.description: Delivers five-star service: earns more at hospitality jobs and runs better events.

syllabus: Week 1: Dubai's tourism economy and the guest journey
Week 2: Front office, housekeeping and service recovery
Week 3: Revenue management: ADR, occupancy and RevPAR
Week 4: Food and beverage, events and the guest bill

weeks.title: Dubai's Tourism Economy
weeks.objective: Understand why Dubai is a global destination and map the guest journey.

slides.title: A City Built for Visitors
slides.body: Tourism is one of Dubai's biggest industries, regulated by the Department of Economy and Tourism (DET). Hotels are classified by DET, and every hotel, holiday home and tour operator needs a licence.
bullets: DET licenses and classifies hotels, hotel apartments and holiday homes
Major demand drivers: events, shopping, beaches, business travel and transit through DXB
Peak season: roughly October to April; summer brings deals and family travel
Ramadan and Eid change hours, menus and demand
slides.takeaway: Know your city's calendar: demand, staffing and prices all follow it.

slides.title: The Guest Journey
slides.body: Great hospitality is designed moment by moment, from the first search to the review after checkout.
bullets: Dreaming and booking: website, OTAs (online travel agencies), reviews
Arrival: airport transfer, welcome, check-in in minutes
The stay: room, food, pool, concierge, personal touches
Departure and after: fast checkout, thank-you message, review request
slides.takeaway: Every touchpoint is a chance to delight or disappoint. Design them all.

lab.title: Guest Journey Lab
lab.brief: Map the full guest journey for a family staying 4 nights at a Dubai beach resort, and find 5 'wow' moments to add.
lab.deliverable: A journey map with touchpoints, pain points and wow moments.
lab.proTip: Small personal touches (a child's name on a welcome note) are remembered for years.

caseStudy.scenario: A five-star hotel's reviews mention long check-in queues at 3pm. What's the best fix?

options.text: Offer online pre-check-in, more agents at peak times, and a welcome drink while guests wait.
options.explanation: Cut the wait and make the wait pleasant.

quiz.question: Who licenses and classifies hotels in Dubai?
quiz.explanation: DET regulates tourism and hotel classification.

quiz.question: Dubai's peak tourism season is roughly:
quiz.explanation: The cooler months bring the most visitors.

weeks.title: Front Office, Housekeeping and Service Recovery
weeks.objective: Run smooth operations and turn complaints into loyalty.

slides.title: Front Office and Housekeeping
slides.body: The front office is the hotel's nerve centre; housekeeping delivers the product guests actually sleep in. They work as one team through room status.
bullets: Room statuses: occupied, vacant dirty, vacant clean, inspected, out of order
Housekeeping targets: rooms cleaned per attendant per shift
Par levels: linen stock of about 3 sets per bed (one in use, one in laundry, one on the shelf)
Lost and found and guest privacy are handled strictly
slides.takeaway: When front office and housekeeping talk, rooms are ready and guests are happy.

slides.title: Service Recovery
slides.body: Things go wrong in every hotel. What matters is the response. Many luxury hotels train staff on a simple model to handle complaints.
bullets: Listen without interrupting
Empathise and apologise sincerely
Resolve it quickly, with the power to act (many brands let staff spend a set amount without asking)
Follow up and record it so it doesn't happen again
slides.takeaway: A complaint fixed brilliantly can create a more loyal guest than no complaint at all.

lab.title: Service Recovery Role-Play
lab.brief: Script responses to 5 common complaints (noisy room, late room, wrong order, broken AC, rude staff) using listen, empathise, resolve, follow up.
lab.deliverable: Five short scripts with the resolution you'd offer.
lab.proTip: Empower your team: the first person a guest speaks to should be able to fix most problems.

caseStudy.scenario: A guest's room isn't ready at 3pm check-in after a long flight. What's the best response?

options.text: Tell them to wait in the lobby until it's ready.
Apologise, store their bags, offer the pool or lounge with a drink, and call them the moment it's ready, or upgrade if one is free.
options.explanation: Turn the wait into comfort, and use upgrades when possible.

options.text: Blame housekeeping in front of them.

quiz.question: What does 'vacant clean' mean?
quiz.explanation: The room is empty and cleaned, awaiting inspection.

quiz.question: A linen par of 3 means:
quiz.explanation: One set in use, one in laundry, one ready.

weeks.title: Revenue Management
weeks.objective: Price rooms to fill the hotel at the best rate.

slides.title: The Key Numbers
slides.body: Hotels measure performance with a few ratios that every manager must know.
bullets: Occupancy % = rooms sold ÷ rooms available
ADR (Average Daily Rate) = room revenue ÷ rooms sold
RevPAR = room revenue ÷ rooms available (or ADR × occupancy)
GOPPAR: gross operating profit per available room
slides.example:
A 200-room hotel sells 150 rooms tonight for AED 120,000 in total.
Occupancy: 150 ÷ 200 = 75%
ADR: 120,000 ÷ 150 = AED 800
RevPAR: 120,000 ÷ 200 = AED 600 (also 800 × 75%)
slides.takeaway: RevPAR combines price and occupancy: it's the number owners watch.

slides.title: Dynamic Pricing and Channels
slides.body: Prices change with demand. Big events like New Year's Eve, Gitex or the Dubai Airshow push rates up; quiet summer nights call for packages and deals.
bullets: Forecast demand from events, bookings and history
Raise rates and set minimum stays in peak periods
Direct bookings save OTA commissions (often 15 to 25%)
Packages add value without cutting the room rate
slides.takeaway: Sell the right room to the right guest at the right price, through the right channel.

lab.title: Revenue Lab
lab.brief: Calculate occupancy, ADR and RevPAR for a week of data, then set prices for a big event weekend.
lab.deliverable: Your calculations and a pricing plan with reasons.
lab.proTip: Don't chase occupancy at any price: a full hotel at a low rate can earn less than a 85% hotel at a strong rate.

caseStudy.scenario: Next month Dubai hosts a huge exhibition and your hotel is 95% booked already at normal rates. What should revenue do?

options.explanation: That leaves money on the table when demand is high.

options.text: Raise rates for the remaining rooms and set a minimum stay.
options.explanation: High demand supports higher rates and longer stays.

weeks.title: Food, Events and the Guest Bill
weeks.objective: Run F&B and events, and understand every line on a Dubai hotel bill.

slides.title: F&B and Events
slides.body: Restaurants, bars, banquets and weddings can bring in a large share of a hotel's revenue. Events need tight planning: BEOs (banquet event orders) tell every department what to do.
bullets: BEO: menu, timings, set-up, AV, staffing for each event
Covers and average spend drive restaurant revenue
Halal food and alcohol licensing rules apply
Weddings and conferences fill hotels in low seasons
slides.takeaway: Events are logistics: one clear BEO keeps 10 departments in step.

slides.title: The Dubai Hotel Bill
slides.body: Dubai hotel bills add charges on top of the room rate, and guests often ask about them. Front office teams must explain each one clearly.
bullets: Service charge: typically 10%
Municipality fee: 7%
VAT: 5%
Tourism Dirham: a fixed fee per room per night, higher for more stars (up to AED 20 a night)
slides.example:
One night at AED 1,000 in a 5-star hotel, roughly:
• Room: AED 1,000
• Service charge 10%: AED 100
• Municipality fee 7%: AED 70
• VAT 5% (on the room and charges): about AED 59
• Tourism Dirham: AED 20
Total: about AED 1,249
slides.takeaway: Explain charges before the guest is surprised by them.

lab.title: Event Plan Lab
lab.brief: Write a BEO for a 150-guest wedding dinner: menu, timings, set-up, staffing and AV.
lab.proTip: Walk the event in your head minute by minute: that's where the gaps show up.

caseStudy.scenario: A guest disputes a 'Tourism Dirham' line on their bill. What do you say?

options.text: It's a hotel extra you can remove.
options.explanation: It's a government fee, not a hotel extra.

options.text: Explain it's a Dubai government fee charged per room per night, collected by every hotel.
options.explanation: Clear, honest explanation of a mandatory fee.

quiz.question: What is a BEO?
options: A banquet event order that guides every department
